clue.text: Corrupt deal, by implication?

parts.note: the word deal is the letters of lead sent wandering, i.e. lead jumbled; so the clue word is what you get by reading the two-word answer as an instruction

explanation.surface: A shady business deal is described as corrupt, with a nudge that it is only implied.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, LEAD sent off course (ASTRAY, an anagram signal), and it produces DEAL, the word in the clue. 'by implication?' flags this backwards reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrupt someone is to tempt them morally off the right path, an idiom for misguiding.

clue.text: Put right about couple

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: An instruction to fix something concerning a pair of people or things.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: mending a fault means making it whole again, i.e. fixing.

clue.text: Very excited over one riding Derby winner

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits over (above) the rest

parts.note: hyper is informal for very excited
I is the Roman numeral for one
riding means on, as a rider is on a horse

explanation.surface: A jockey, thrilled at being aboard, rides a horse to victory in the Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's most famous flat horse race, run at Epsom; Hyperion won it in 1933.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the horse of that name won the Epsom Derby in 1933, so it is a famous winner of the race.

clue.text: Take up space in dock

indicators.note: in a down clue, take up means read the word for space upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: room means space

explanation.surface: A ship occupying a berth in the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to tie a boat up at a quay is to bring it into harbour and secure it.

clue.text: London landmark, indistinct during parade

indicators.note: during means the word for indistinct goes into the middle of the word for parade

parts.note: a march is a parade
blear means dim or indistinct

explanation.surface: A London monument seen blurred while a procession passes.
explanation.walkthrough: MARBLE ARCH is a white triumphal arch at the west end of Oxford Street, London.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the arch is a well-known monument near Hyde Park in the capital.

clue.text: Confused, a theologian left editor

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A muddled theologian walks out on his editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a muddled mind is one that is befuddled and not thinking clearly.

clue.text: Name murdered snitcher

indicators.note: murdered signals the letters of snitcher being mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Identify the informer who was killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to baptise a child is to give it a name formally.

clue.text: Soon rule Conservative out

indicators.note: out means the letter for Conservative is removed from the word for rule

parts.note: a canon is a rule or principle

explanation.surface: A prediction that a Tory will shortly be excluded from governing.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic synonym: the word means shortly or presently, as in 'I'll see you presently'.

clue.text: English extremely negative — stick therefore follows, from time to time

indicators.note: follows says the stick and therefore come after the earlier pieces

parts.note: very means extremely
no is a negative
a wand is a stick
then can mean therefore, as in 'then we agree'

explanation.surface: A logic-chopping sentence about an Englishman's very negative stick and its consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something that happens occasionally happens at intervals, not regularly.

clue.text: Navigator, duke, and playboy

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute playboy

explanation.surface: A list of three types: a sailor, a nobleman and a womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan seaman who circumnavigated the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Elizabethan seaman sailed around the world, a famous explorer at sea.

clue.text: Beer off? Flipping poorly on rising

indicators.note: beer that has gone off is spoilt, so its letters are spoilt into a new order
flipping means the word for poorly is turned back to front

parts.note: poorly means ill

explanation.surface: Someone feeling unwell after drinking beer that has turned sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' sits at the end looking like part of the surface, but it is the definition, in its noun sense of a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a rising is an uprising or revolt against authority.

clue.text: Slavery in novel riveted us

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of riveted us form a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A novel about slavery gripped its readers.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being in bondage, forced to serve a master, is slavery.

clue.text: Incredible lunacy involving Welshman in play?

indicators.note: involving means the jumbled letters wrap around the Welshman
incredible signals the letters of lunacy rearranged beyond belief

parts.note: Evan is a typical Welsh man's name

explanation.surface: A play involving a Welshman that is unbelievably mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Uncle Vanya is a drama by Anton Chekhov.

clue.text: To put off, in crude terms

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the words crude terms

explanation.surface: To discourage someone using rough language.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to discourage someone from acting is to dissuade them.

clue.text: Magnificent having lots of money in hand

parts.note: royal means magnificent or splendid
flush means well supplied with cash

explanation.surface: A magnificent rich person holding something in their hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in poker, the best possible hand is ace to ten of a single suit.

clue.text: Sure-fire winner? Cite Cary Grant in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, as seed is broadcast, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A broadcaster mentions the film star Cary Grant as a guaranteed hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' that looks like a link word is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a horse thought certain to win a race, hence anything bound to succeed.

clue.text: What Acker Bilk played may be popular in Bordeaux

indicators.note: in means the word for popular goes inside the word for Bordeaux

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Acker Bilk's music might be a hit in Bordeaux.
explanation.walkthrough: Acker Bilk was an English jazz musician known for 'Stranger on the Shore'. 'Bordeaux' looks like the city but is its wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Bilk was famous as a player of this woodwind instrument.

clue.text: A jolly cleaner skirting one item of furniture

parts.note: a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

indicators.note: skirting means the word for cleaner goes around the letter for one

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cheerful cleaner dusting around a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is British for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an upholstered seat with side supports is a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Poet sure to receive a first from Trinity

indicators.note: to receive means the word for sure takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: sure means yes, as in agreement

indicators.note: first from means the opening letter of Trinity

explanation.surface: A poet is sure to be awarded a first-class degree from Trinity College.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: W. B. Yeats was an Irish poet and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Colas I ordered for party

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of Colas I are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Soft drinks requested for a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a social is an informal gathering or get-together.

clue.text: Power held by male here, surprisingly short-lived

indicators.note: held by means the letter for power is placed among the letters of male here
surprisingly signals the combined letters rearranged unexpectedly

explanation.surface: A man here holding power briefly, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something transient lasts only a brief time, like a mayfly.

clue.text: The little auk Hector trained

indicators.note: trained means the letters of Hector are drilled into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone called Hector has trained a small seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialect bird name: an old name for this small Arctic seabird, the dovekie.

clue.text: Disturb bats, distraught because of prolonged confinement

parts.note: to stir is to disturb
bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Disturbing bats in a cave until they are frantic from being shut in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals but is slang for mad. Stir is also slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a prisoner going mad from long imprisonment, hence frantic at being cooped up.

clue.text: Location shown in news item

indicators.note: shown in means the answer is displayed within the words news item

explanation.surface: A place named in a news report.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a site is a place where something is situated.

clue.text: Period of time — long? short?

indicators.note: short means the word for long loses its final letter

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a span of time is long or short.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: twelve months make up this unit of time.

clue.text: Inn very popular with the Spanish

parts.note: hot means very popular, as a hot ticket
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A tavern that is a favourite with Spanish visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are establishments offering lodging to travellers.

clue.text: Film magazine awfully vain female's after

indicators.note: after places the female's piece at the end

parts.note: The Lady is a long-running British weekly magazine

indicators.note: awfully signals the letters of vain arranged badly

parts.note: she's is a contraction of she is, a female's

explanation.surface: A magazine piece about a terribly vain woman.
explanation.walkthrough: THE LADY is a British weekly magazine; 'awfully' turns VAIN into VANI.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: The Lady Vanishes is a 1938 Hitchcock thriller.
